variables.reason: The typed ledger defines Ra as "the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations." The retrieved record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness is the canonical definition for arithmetic mean roughness (symbols Ra, R_a) with definition "Mean absolute deviation of surface height from its mean level" and si_dimension: L (si_unit: m). That entry directly identifies Ra as a length-scale roughness statistic, supporting the proposed SI exponents (L=1, all other bases =0).

The typed ledger defines kt as "the peak-to-valley height." The retrieved record pq_peak_to_valley_height explicitly defines mean peak-to-valley roughness height (symbols including kt) as a roughness-amplitude measure formed from vertical height differences; si_dimension: L (si_unit: m). This directly ties kt to a length dimension, validating the candidate exponents (L=1).

The typed ledger gives k_rms as "the root-mean-square height." The retrieved record pq_rms_roughness_height defines root-mean-square roughness height (symbols k_rms) as the RMS fluctuation of surface height about its mean and lists si_dimension: L (si_unit: m). That shows k_rms is a length-scale and supports the exponents (L=1).

The typed ledger defines Sk as "the skewness of roughness height fluctuations." The retrieved record pq_height_skewness defines surface-height skewness (symbols Sk) as the third standardized moment of the surface-height distribution and explicitly labels si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). This confirms Sk carries no base SI dimensions and justifies all-zero exponents.

The typed ledger gives Ku as "the kurtosis of roughness height fluctuations." The retrieved record pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (symbols Ku) as the fourth standardized moment of the height distribution and lists si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). That record applies to Ku in the original problem and supports the all-zero SI exponents.

The typed ledger describes ES as "the effective streamwise slope of the roughness." The retrieved record pq_effective_surface_slope defines effective surface slope (symbols ES) as a mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction and explicitly notes a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and therefore dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). This justifies ES having all-zero SI exponents.

The typed ledger lists Po as "the surface porosity." The retrieved record pq_porosity defines porosity (symbols Po) as a fraction of void or open volume/area and explicitly gives si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). That record applies to the surface porosity used in this roughness problem and supports the all-zero SI exponents.
